newsitem.title: KENYA: 115,000 Rwandan refugees leave east Zaire camp.
newsitem.headline: 115,000 Rwandan refugees leave east Zaire camp.

text.p: An estimated 115,000 Rwandan refugees abandoned Kahindo camp in eastern Zaire because of security problems on Wednesday and started moving to a camp already crammed with 400,000 people, aid workers said.

"The whole population of Kahindo camp, 115,000 people, is on the move. It appears they packed up in the past few hours and started moving towards Mugunga camp," said Michelle Quintaglie, a spokeswoman for the U.N. World Food Programme in Goma city.

"We hear reports there were security problems in the area over the past few hours," said Quintaglie, adding that they would have to move through Virunga National Park on the way to Mugunga camp, about 50 km (30 miles) southwest of Kahindo.
"If these people arrive in Mugunga we will have a major, major problem on our hands. We already have 400,000 in Mugunga and the arrival of such a large number could be chaotic," she told Reuters.
Shelling and shooting in Kibumba camp on Friday night and Saturday prompted the 200,000 refugees there to flee to Mugunga, west of Goma city, on Saturday, swelling its population to some 400,000.
